# Creator survey: what would make Frame Job a leading creator editor

## Summary

This survey is dated 1 November 2026. It asks what would make Frame Job a leading editor for content creators. It draws on five inputs:

- an inventory of the tree;
- four research sweeps (creator tools, pro editors, screen and tutorial tools, creator demand);
- three strategists' proposals;
- the candidates merged from those proposals;
- adversarial checks of each candidate against the code, Apple's frameworks and the market.

Frame Job is already ahead of most creator tools on finishing: its audio chain, colour and HDR, codecs, and an MCP surface that covers the whole editor. It loses creators earlier, at the jobs that now define a creator editor:

- cutting a talk by its transcript;
- polishing a screen recording from the cursor;
- turning a horizontal edit into vertical shorts;
- finding the clips worth posting;
- switching podcast angles by speaker;
- cutting the presenter out of the background.

Agent access no longer sets a tool apart, because most AI-forward editors gained an MCP server in 2026. No rival combines what Frame Job has: a full editor whose every edit is a pure, undoable op, analysis that runs on the creator's Mac, and AI on the creator's own key with no credits.

The recommendation is to ship those creator jobs as on-device commands whose results land as ordinary edits on the timeline, in the order below. The rest is either table stakes to pick up later or not worth chasing.

## What Frame Job has

Frame Job is a native macOS editor for Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or later. It is a Swift/AppKit app over a Rust core, Apache-2.0, with no account and no backend. As of 1 November 2026 it has the following.

- **Editing.** One kind of track. Move, trim, slip, roll, rate-stretch, split, lift, ripple delete, insert and overwrite. Nests. Picture and sound linked for J- and L-cuts. Markers with a chapter flag. A second preview window. Every edit is one undo step through one mutation point, and a refused edit says why in the rule's own sentence.
- **Picture.** Transform, crop, blend modes, chroma key, spotlight, obscure regions, text with reveals, shapes with gradients, blurred backgrounds, and matte tracks that let any clip cut the track behind it. Actions animate almost every property, including speed, which is how speed ramps work. 13 transitions, and Zoom to Region for screencasts.
- **Audio.**
  - A per-clip chain: voice isolation, EQ, hum and noise reduction, gate, a phrase-level leveller, de-esser, compressor and true-peak limiter.
  - Enhance Voice, Match Audio, Normalize to LUFS, Duck by Speech, and Synchronize Audio with drift correction.
  - Track compressor and limiter, a live loudness meter, stems, and a −1 dBTP master on every export.
- **Clean-up.** Remove Silences (on-device Silero VAD), Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI word timings; cloud-only), and `get_transcript`. The Assistant cuts false starts when asked.
- **Captions.** On-device or AssemblyAI transcription. Subtitles plus five word-by-word styles and three looks. SRT and WebVTT export; SRT import.
- **Colour and HDR.**
  - Grading: wheels, curves, hue curves, looks, .cube LUTs, adjustment clips with qualifiers, and four scopes.
  - Log footage: Apple Log (detected on import), S-Log3, V-Log and Canon log.
  - HDR: HLG projects with HLG, HDR10 and SDR deliverables, on a 16-bit float compositor.
- **Graphics.** Sandboxed JavaScript modules that return SVG per frame, 23 bundled templates, shareable `.fjgraphic` packages, and agents that write new graphics.
- **Recording.** A display or a window through ScreenCaptureKit, with system audio, a separate microphone file, click rings, pause and resume, a camera beside the screen (bottom-right), and voice-over.
- **Export.** H.264, HEVC (10-bit and with alpha), AV1 and VP9 through bundled encoders, ProRes, audio formats and stems, GIF, APNG and stills. An Export Queue, embedded chapters, and loudness targets of −14 and −16 LUFS.
- **Agents.** 106 product tools over a local socket (one per edit, plus app-state tools), the bundled `framejob-mcp` helper, and `render_frame` so an agent can look at its work. An in-app Assistant runs on the creator's own Anthropic key and shows its spend.

### Where it is already ahead

- The whole editor is exposed as MCP tools printed from the core's own op table. Every agent edit is an undo step shown live, and `render_frame` lets an agent check its work.
- Its audio chain is deeper than any creator tool surveyed: a leveller, de-esser, true-peak master, LUFS targets, stems, Synchronize Audio with drift correction, and Duck by Speech.
- Colour management and HDR deliverables (HLG, HDR10, an SDR version) and log support. Creator tools lack these.
- Codec breadth: AV1 and VP9 with bundled encoders, VP9 and HEVC with alpha, ProRes 4444, and WebM and MKV import without re-encoding.
- A programmable motion-graphics engine whose templates agents can write.
- Open source with bring-your-own key and on-device processing first: no credits, no subscription, no upload of footage.

### What creators ask for

- **Editing is the biggest time sink.** One vendor classified 27,555 comments on 44 creator-education channels. Editing and production was the largest category, at 21.4% of actionable comments, ahead of monetisation at 15.6% [D1]. This is one vendor's analysis, not a survey.
- **Most work alone, and repurposing is wanted.** In Adobe Express's survey of 384 US video creators (December 2025), 86% work solo. The most-wanted new AI features were auto-repurposing (19%), instant platform-specific edits (14%) and help while filming (14%) [D2].
- **AI use is near-universal, but cost and training worry them.** In Adobe's 2025 Creators' Toolkit (more than 16,000 creators, 8 countries), 86% use generative AI. High cost is the top barrier, at 38%, and 69% worry their content will train AI without permission [D3].
- **They want control over agents.** In Adobe's 2026 report, 85% say the final decision must stay with the creator. Among creators who want more agent independence, 44% want to review, edit or undo at any point, and 37% want to see what the agent is doing and why. 57% say AI output usually needs moderate or extensive editing [D4]. Epidemic Sound found 94% use AI and 89% feel pressure to [D5].
- **Video podcasts are big and the picture edit is still manual.**
  - YouTube reports over 1 billion monthly podcast users [D10]. Spotify says more than 500 million users have streamed a video podcast [D11]. Edison found 57% of Americans 12+ have both listened to and watched a podcast [D12].
  - Automatic angle switching has long-open Premiere idea threads [D13] and is sold as AutoPod for about $29 a month [D14].
  - Descript users ask for multicam export to Final Cut Pro and Premiere (181 votes) [D6].
- **Descript frustrations.** The top requests are regenerating speech in more languages (753 votes), an iOS/iPadOS app (417), transcription in more languages (400) and strip silence (192) [D6]. Reviewers report slow scrubbing and long exports [D8]. Plans moved to media minutes plus AI credits with no rollover [D7].
- **Captions.** Premiere's animated-caption request has about 416 votes, and users round-trip to CapCut [D15]. A verifier counted about 380. Either way, the request is for animated word captions, which Frame Job already has.
- **Auto-cutters are distrusted.** Riverside Magic Clips is faulted for cutting where a thought ends rather than where the energy peaks [D16]. Gling sometimes cuts good takes [D17].
- **What makes creators switch tools:**
  - price rises and forced subscriptions [C5] [D19] [S7];
  - content-licence scares [D18];
  - stability regressions [D20];
  - metered AI credits [P7] [D7].
- **Platform rules a tool can check.**
  - YouTube chapters start at 00:00, need at least three, and each must be at least 10 s [D21].
  - Apple Podcasts asks for about −16 LKFS with a true peak at or below −1 dBFS [D22].
  - Spotify video podcasts want H.264, 16:9 and Rec.709 with stereo AAC, and HDR is tone-mapped to SDR [D23].
  - No platform publishes safe-zone figures, and third-party figures conflict [D24].
  - YouTube requires disclosure of realistic synthetic content but exempts colour fixes, background blur, captions and audio repair [D25].
- **Platforms build the simple cases themselves.** YouTube's own clips tool suggests moments only in 10 countries and 7 languages [D9]. Twitch is building vertical streaming (beta) and Auto Clips with captions (waitlist) [D26].

## The bets

The bets are ranked by how many creators each reaches, how often they would use it, and how far it puts Frame Job ahead rather than level, discounted by effort and risk.

Every bet has the same shape. Analysis that Frame Job already caches, or that macOS provides on the device, feeds a planner. The planner writes edits the core already knows how to make. Each result is therefore an ordinary undo step on a real timeline, and each command becomes an MCP tool that the Assistant and outside agents can run with no new agent work.

Effort is build effort (S, M, L, XL), never lines of code.

| Rank | Bet | Effort | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript tab | L | Everyone who records themselves talking |
| 2 | Screen recordings with the cursor as data | L | Screencasts, tutorials, courses, product demos |
| 3 | Make Vertical Version | M (copy), L (linked versions) | Everyone who posts shorts |
| 4 | Find Clips | M on top of 3 | Podcasters, long-form YouTubers, streamers |
| 5 | Switch by Speaker, and every audio track | M | Video podcasts and interviews |
| 6 | Camera cutout and layouts | L | Screencasters, talking heads, streamers |

Bets 1 and 2 remove the two points where talking creators and the home segment give up. Bets 3 and 4 complete the long-to-short loop. Bet 5 takes the podcast format on the strength of the audio chain. Bet 6 closes the presenter-camera gap.

### 1. Transcript tab: cut by deleting words, with retakes found for review

**Pitch.** A Transcript tab shows the timeline's words in timeline order. The word being spoken is highlighted during playback, and clicking a word moves the playhead to it. The creator selects a sentence and presses Delete, and that span ripples out of the video as one undo step. Cut words stay greyed in place and can be restored.

A review pass strikes through long pauses and, where an AssemblyAI transcript exists, filler words. After the §11 decision below, it also strikes earlier takes of each repeated line and false starts. One click removes everything struck, as one undo step. Words inside a nest or a transition overlap show as not editable, with the reason.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** On its own this brings Frame Job level. Editing by transcript ships in:

- Descript [C7], Screen Studio 4 [S4] and Tella [S11];

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Opened 2026-10-30** (AP0), when the owner answered the five choices below ("Yes, lift scopes,
and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the rest): AU-2…AU-4, and spec
§1's audio non-goal lifted. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (answered 2026-10-30: all five as recommended)

Recorded as AU-2 (choice 1), AU-3 (choices 4 and 5) and AU-4 (choices 2 and 3). The owner,
on the rest: "We'll address other questions as we progress. If builds can be run in multiple
lanes, do so."

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*

Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement:** this worktree is the integration branch; each phase is built
  through litecode in a lane of its own, gated, committed, rebased onto the integration branch
  one at a time and gated again there, as codec-export (CX-11) and grading (GR-25) merged
  phase by phase. Merging into main is done from the main checkout.
- **Lanes (the owner's "multiple lanes"):** after AP0, at most three at once, split by the
  files they touch. **Lane A, the voice block:** AP1 → AP2 → AP3 → AP4 → AP5 → AP6, then AP8
  and AP14, which build on its stages. **Lane B, editing and playback:** AP9 → AP13 → AP7
  (the meter after AP1 has landed, since both read `Loudness.swift`). **Lane C, the mix:**
  AP11 → AP10 (after AP2 has landed: both work in the export's float gain stage) → AP12
  (after AP3). A lane whose next phase waits on another lane's phase waits; it never builds
  against an unlanded one.
- **Collisions between lanes:** each phase numbers its decisions in its own block (APn's
  AU-n0…, AU-2's note), and a format bump is provisional until its phase lands: the
  integrator renumbers it (and its `schema_vN.rs`) when another lane landed one first.
- **Agent parity:** every new property is a `set_audio` key, every new command a tool, every
  new answer readable through `get_project`.
- **Proof currency:** exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic
  (`phase5_proof.py`'s BS.1770 and 4× true-peak oversampler), synthetic fixtures with known
  answers, and the owner's samples where present. What only ears can judge is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **Samples:** the owner records the survey's §6 list. A phase uses a sample when it exists and
  a synthetic fixture otherwise; no phase waits for one.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults and bump the format (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older
  project opens unchanged and sounds the same.

## How it fits the tree (at `33eeed0`)

- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's
  settings by span (`AudioDSPSpan`). `AudioDSP.swift` (**890, over the cap**) holds pan, the mono
  fold, the compressor (default threshold −18 dB) and noise reduction, real-time safe. Volume,
  fades and ducking come after the tap, as the core's envelope played as volume ramps
  (`core/src/audio.rs` 537, `audio_duck.rs` 136). **A new live stage sees the clip at its
  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).
  The export measures a 32-bit float mix and gains it in `ExporterAudioGain.swift` (179); its
  write pass still decodes 16-bit integers (#86).
- **Offline renders have a pattern.** Speed-ramp audio renders into `cache/ramp-audio/` through
  `RampAudioRenders` (a serial queue, owners, a wait in the export, dry while pending).
- **Loudness exists once.** `Loudness.swift` (**674, over the cap**) is BS.1770-4 for the
  export; `ExporterLoudness.swift` (211) its measurement pass.
- **The model.** `AudioProps` lives in `core/src/model_props.rs` (551), checked by
  `props_check.rs` (526) and clamped by `actions_clamp.rs` (386); pan, mono, compressor, noise
  reduction, duck and keep pitch are BASE-only (`InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`'s
  `structural(audio:)`), and only volume, mute and the fades animate.
- **Caches.** Peaks, sync features and speech (Silero VAD) per media, on the cache lane
  (`MediaCacheLane.swift`); a loudness cache would be a fifth beside them.

## Phases

| Phase | Survey items | What a person gets |
|---|---|---|
| AP0 | — | Scope lifted, the spike's answers, the files split |
| AP1 | A2, A8 (readout) | A clip's LUFS shown; Normalize to a loudness |
| AP2 | A1, A13 | A true-peak limiter; the export reaches its loudness; 24-bit |
| AP3 | A3, A7, B7 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, channel selection |
| AP4 | A5, A6 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
| AP5 | A4, B4 | Voice isolation; de-reverb if isolation does it |
| AP6 | B1, B3, B8 | Enhance Voice; the leveller; clean-up when a voice-over lands |
| AP7 | A8 | Live LUFS and true-peak meter |
| AP8 | A9 | Every audio parameter animates; the volume line on the clip |
| AP9 | A10 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; reversible Detach |
| AP10 | A12, A11 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
| AP11 | B2, B9 | Ducking by speech; fade and crossfade shapes |
| AP12 | B6 | Match one clip's level and tone to another |
| AP13 | B5 | Audio while scrubbing |
| AP14 | B10 | Voice effects (E8, #123) |

AP1–AP6 are the voice block, in the order the owner's recording needs them. AP7 onward is the
mixing block and can be reordered freely; only AP12 needs AP3, and AP6 needs AP2–AP5.

### AP0 — scope, the record, the tolls and the spike

- **Decisions:** AU-2 (the scope, from choice 1), AU-3 (the chain, choices 4 and 5), AU-4 (the
  loudness defaults, choices 2 and 3). Spec §1's non-goal sentence rewritten; this road map
  opened.
- **Tolls, each a pure move landed and gated alone:** `AudioDSP.swift` cut at its MARKs (the
  compressor and noise reduction into their own files, the chain kept); `AudioTap.swift`'s
  schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the

schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the
  cap; `AudioProps` and its vocabulary out of `model_props.rs` into a new `model_audio.rs`.
- **Spike S, its rule fixed before its run, its record here:**
  - **S1 — own DSP or Apple units, live.** A biquad EQ and Frame Job's limiter against
    `AVAudioUnitEQ`, `AUNBandEQ` and `AUPeakLimiter` driven inside the tap: byte-identical
    exports run twice, preview against export, CPU per track at eight stages, latency.
  - **S2 — voice isolation.** `AUSoundIsolation` rendered offline over the owner's recording:
    speed against real time, latency, determinism across runs, the pause floor and the speech
    band against the shipped noise reducer, and whether it reduces reverberation (B4's
    question), on a reverberant sample if one exists.
  - **S3 — tracks and the master in the preview.** Whether one composition audio track ever
    carries two timeline tracks; the error of a track chain run per composition track during an
    overlap (zero for linear stages, measured for dynamics); the options for a preview master
    limiter (none and say so, per-track, or an offline premix); rebuilding the true mix from the
    taps for a LUFS meter.
  - **S4 — a loudness cache.** K-weighted 100 ms block energies per media: size, build time on
    a 20-minute file, and integrated LUFS over any window against `Loudness.swift` measuring an
    export of the same window (agreement within 0.1 LU).
- **Acceptance:** `make gate` after each toll; the spike's verdicts recorded here.

### AP1 — loudness you can see and target (A2, A8's readout)

- A per-media loudness cache (`cache/loudness/<id>.bin`, S4's format) on the cache lane after
  peaks, current by `CacheStamp` like the others.
- The Volume section reads the clip's integrated loudness (gated, over the window that plays)
  and its true peak beside the Gain row.
- Normalize gains a **Loudness** mode: a target in LUFS, each clip of a selection to the same
  target, which is what "match these clips" means. Until AP2, a clip whose peak would pass the
  ceiling stops short and says where it landed, as the volume ceiling does today.
  `normalize_clip` gains `mode` and `target_lufs`.
- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;
  the owner's recording; a selection of two levels landing equal.

### AP2 — limiters, and an export that reaches its loudness (A1, A13)

- A **clip limiter** stage in the tap: lookahead, 4× oversampled true-peak detection, a ceiling
  in dBTP. Because the fader is downstream, the stage is told the clip's gain (decision AU-n:
  the base volume, with fades and ducks only ever lowering it), and its lookahead is a lead
  like noise reduction's (SY-25).
- The **export:** a float decode before the gain (#86, closing it), a master limiter in the
  float write pass so the loudness target limits instead of capping, and an `audio_bits` choice
  of 16 or 24 on WAV and AIFF.
- Loudness Normalize uses the clip limiter, so the owner's recording reaches −16 LUFS at
  −1 dBTP. If choice 2 says so, Loudness becomes the button's default here.
- **Proof:** every export's true peak at or under its ceiling by the proof's oversampler; the
  loudness target met within ±0.5 LU on `phase5_proof.py`'s crest fixture, which today lands
  quieter; a 24-bit file decoded with its low bits used; the owner's recording.
- **Manual check:** no pumping or distortion on speech and on music.
- **Built in two parts, by size.** Part 1: the clip limiter, `audio.limiter` (format 30), its
  Limiter section and `set_audio` key, and Loudness Normalize through it as the default
  (AU-20…AU-26; its record below). Part 2: the export's float decode (#86), the master limiter
  in the float write pass and `audio_bits` (AU-27 on).

### AP3 — EQ, hum removal and channel selection (A3, A7, B7)

- **EQ:** a high-pass with a slope, a low-pass, low and high shelves and a number of parametric
  bands (set at AP3), with voice presets (rumble cut, de-mud, presence). An EQ section in the
  Sound sub-tab with the response curve drawn.
- **Hum:** notches at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, depth and harmonic count.
- **Channels:** both, left only, right only, swapped, before the mono fold, so a mic recorded
  on one channel of a stereo file plays at its level.
- **Model:** `audio.eq`, `audio.hum`, `audio.channels`; format bump; MCP keys.
- **Proof:** tones and sweeps through each band against the biquad's analytic response
  (±0.1 dB); notch depth at each harmonic; a channel pick sample-identical to its source channel.

### AP4 — gate, expander and de-esser (A5, A6)

- A downward **expander/gate** sharing the compressor's envelope follower: threshold relative
  to the clip's measured level (AP1), ratio, range, attack, hold, release.
- A **de-esser:** a compressor keyed on a high band (frequency, threshold, range).
- **Model, inspector, MCP** as AP3; format bump.
- **Proof:** a tone burst over noise, the pause floor lowered by the range and the burst
  untouched; sibilant noise bursts reduced in band and the voice band untouched; the owner's
  recording's pause floor.

### AP5 — voice isolation (A4; B4's verdict)

- **Isolation** by `AUSoundIsolation` (S2), rendered offline per clip window into
  `cache/isolated/` on the ramp-audio pattern: an Amount (wet/dry), dry while pending, the
  export waiting for its render, re-rendered when the window or the file changes.
- **De-reverb (B4):** if S2 measured reverberation removed, it is this control and the guide
  says so; otherwise B4 is filed with tier C and the measurement.
- **Proof:** the render aligned with the dry clip within a sample (cross-correlation); the pause
  floor and the speech band against the dry clip; dry while pending; an export that waits.
- **Manual check:** artefacts on the owner's voice at Amount 100 % and 50 %.

### AP6 — Enhance Voice, the leveller, and clean-up when a voice-over lands (B1, B3, B8)

- **Enhance Voice** (Clip menu, a button in the Sound sub-tab, an `enhance_voice` tool): reads
  the clip's loudness, its peak and the noise floor over the VAD cache's non-speech spans, then
  writes ORDINARY settings a person can see and change — high-pass, isolation or noise
  reduction, gate, de-esser if the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own
  level, the limiter and the loudness target. One undo step; pressing it twice changes nothing.
- **Leveller (B3):** a slow gain-rider stage for a speaker who moves on and off the mic, off by
  default, turned on by Enhance Voice when the speech's short-term loudness range calls for it.
- **At record time (B8):** a recorder setting, "Enhance the microphone when it lands", applying
  Enhance Voice to the Microphone clip after the landing, as its own undo step (AU-68).
- **Proof:** the owner's recording to −16 LUFS ±0.5 at −1 dBTP with its pause floor lowered;
  idempotence; one undo step; a voice-over that lands enhanced.
- **Built in three parts, by size, as AP2 was.** Part 1: Enhance Voice itself — the measurements,
  the rules, the loudness cache's high band (version 2), the volume solved on the clip rendered
  through its own chain for Enhance and Loudness Normalize alike (the owner's answer,
  2026-10-31), the Measuring Sound sheet, the button, Clip ▸ Enhance Voice and `enhance_voice`
  (AU-60…AU-65; its record below). Part 2: the leveller, `audio.leveller` (a format bump) — after the
  owner's answer of 2026-10-31 a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's loudness and
  speech and applied with no state in the tap — its section, and Enhance turning it on from the
  speech's short-term loudness range (AU-66, AU-67; its record below). Part 3:
  "Enhance the microphone when it lands", the recorder setting and its `UserDefaults` key,
  applied after the landing as its own undo step (AU-68, AU-69; its record below).

### AP7 — live loudness and true-peak metering (A8)

- Momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and true peak while playing, over the true mix
  (S3's method), with a reset; the per-clip readout is AP1's.
- **Proof:** a probe compiled from `app/Sources` fed EBU Tech 3341's test signals, each within
  its tolerance.

### AP8 — every audio parameter animates; the volume line (A9)

Built in two parts once the owner answered the question below with (a), actions (2026-10-30,
AU-80): **AP8a** the volume line, app-only (AU-80…AU-84); **AP8b** every other audio parameter as
action ends through the same model (AU-85…).

- **AP8b:** pan, EQ gains and frequencies, gate, de-esser, compressor and limiter settings,
  isolation's Amount and the leveller's target as action ends; the tap's schedule carries
  per-parameter ramps from the core, not one constant per span. Switches (a stage on or off)
  still change at an action's end, as booleans do (§5.4).
- **AP8a, the volume line:** each clip draws its envelope over its waveform; dragging it edits the
  level. **Asked at AP8:** edit through actions (a point is an action's end, which keeps §2's
  "Actions, not keyframes"; recommended) or add keyframes (lifting it). Answered (a).
- **Proof:** the line drawn where the plan's ramps are (AP8a); exports of an animated pan and EQ
  against analytic gains (AP8b).

### AP9 — split edits (A10)

- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, and Detach Audio made reversible (Attach Audio).
- **Asked at AP9:** a LINKED pair — Detach's two clips carrying one link id, moved, cut and
  deleted together, with ⌥-drag trimming one half alone (recommended: it fits one kind of
  track, and an audio lead on its own track cannot collide with "overlap is a transition") —
  or one clip whose audio window extends past its picture.
- **Proof:** core tests of every edit on a linked pair; exports with the audio leading and
  trailing the picture by a known amount.

### AP10 — tracks, buses and stems (A12, A11)

- A **track fader and pan** in the header and the Track menu (an envelope term in the core, as
  a track's mute is).
- **Track and master processing** by S3's verdict, asked at AP10: the master limiter in the
  export at least; in the preview, as S3 found possible, or said plainly where it differs.
- **Stems:** each track, or a chosen set, as its own file in one export; **asked at AP10:**
  separate files (recommended) or a multitrack movie if S3 measured it to work.
- **Proof:** fader arithmetic on an export; the stems summed against the full mix (a null within
  quantisation when no master dynamics run).

### AP11 — ducking by speech, and fade shapes (B2, B9)

- **Ducking by speech:** the ducking clip's speech spans from the VAD cache, with pre-roll, hold
  and release, drawn as the envelope it makes. **Asked at AP11:** spans persisted on the media
  (a detected field, as Camera Log's is; recommended, so the plan stays a function of the
  project) or handed to the plan by the host.
- **Fade and crossfade shapes:** linear, S-curve, +3 dB and −3 dB, sampled by the core like an
  eased action.
- **Proof:** the plan's ramps against fixture spans; exports of each fade shape against its
  formula.

### AP12 — match one clip to another (B6)

- **Match Loudness** to a reference clip (AP1's measurement) and **Match EQ:** the reference's
  and the target's average speech spectra fitted to AP3's bands. A command and a tool.
- **Proof:** pink noise tilted by a known EQ matched back within ±1 dB a band.

### AP13 — audio while scrubbing (B5)

- Short grains of the mix at the scrub position while the playhead is dragged, off when the
  drag stops; the design is set at AP13 against what AVFoundation allows.
- **Proof:** a probe of the grain scheduler. **Manual check:** the feel, and no clicks.

### AP14 — voice effects (B10, E8)

- E8 as designed and measured (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, #123): sixteen kinds as fixed
  chains of Apple units rendered offline, with an amount and a pitch. Closes #123.

### AP0's record (2026-10-30)

**Landed.** `9e47f56`: the survey, this plan, AU-2…AU-4 and spec §1's audio non-goal lifted. The
tolls, each a pure move gated alone (PASS 307, 246, 243 and 136 s) and checked line-identical
against `9e47f56`: `c67ccee` (`AudioDSP.swift` 890 → 368; `AudioCompressorStage.swift` 158,
`AudioNoiseReductionStage.swift` 376), `54e4649` (`AudioTap.swift` 595 → 328;
`AudioTapSchedule.swift` 273), `a0eb094` (`Loudness.swift` 674 → 511; `ExportLoudness.swift` 168,
which `phase5_chrome.py`'s section 9 now compiles too), `6a51bfc` (`model_props.rs` 551 → 459;
`model_audio.rs` 114); the map entries `fec5132`.

README.md
      47 designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md
# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

content.content:
# 2. The six ideas, and why the model stays simple

Six ideas do most of the work. Frame Job is built on all six.

1. **One kind of track.** Every track holds any clip — video, audio,
   still, text, shape. There are no video-vs-audio track types; an
   audio-only clip simply draws a waveform. Higher track = in front.
2. **A fixed canvas with direct manipulation.** The document has a size
   (1920×1080 by default). Clips are placed on it by dragging on the
   preview; scale, position, rotation and crop are clip properties with
   numbers in the inspector and handles on the canvas.
3. **Actions, not keyframes.** An Action is a span on a clip with an
   easing curve. You edit the property values at the *end* of the span;
   the values at the start are whatever was already in effect. There is
   no keyframe graph.
4. **Overlap is a transition.** Sliding one clip over its neighbour on
   the same track makes a transition of that length. No transition
   track, no browser to drag from.
5. **One inspector, tabbed by what the selection is.** Video / Audio /
   Text / Shape for the selected clip; Media and Document always.
6. **A small keyboard vocabulary.** ⌘T split, W/E trim to playhead,
   ⌘⌫ ripple delete, ⇧⌘F freeze frame, M marker, Space/JKL transport.

Left out: everything that only makes sense for a recording
it made itself (mouse/keyboard/touch callouts, pointer effects), templates,
publishing to YouTube/Vimeo, the stock-media library.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Camera recording (road map "camera-recording")

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The road map that made these is closed (2026-10-27): its condensed record is
`designs/adr/camera-recording.md`, the original `archive/camera-recording.md`. Its parent design
is road map 3 (`designs/adr/roadmap-03-screen-recording.md`), whose decisions in
[`recording.md`](recording.md) stand unless an entry here amends one. CAM-7 onwards are in
[`camera-recording-2.md`](camera-recording-2.md), split from this file at the close by the
spec's ~500-line rule; the IDs are one series. CAM-1 and CAM-2 were recorded in CR0, before any
product code and before the spike's measured run. Each later phase recorded its rule in this
series (CAM-3 on), before its code.

- **CAM-1 — Camera recording is IN; callouts stay OUT** (the owner, 2026-10-26, reversing the
  camera half of recording.md's first bullet and §1's non-goal). Frame Job records a camera on
  its own, or at the same time as a screen recording (a talking head over a screencast). The
  owner's four answers, as given:
  1. **Camera alone, or camera at the same time as a screen recording.** Each capture lands as
     its own file on its own track. With a screen recording the camera goes on a track ABOVE
     the screen, placed as a corner picture-in-picture that can be moved; the corner, the scale
     and the inset are CR3's to decide.
  2. **The entry is the existing recorder panel**: a Camera source, and a camera row when
     recording the screen. One panel, one countdown, one menu-bar status item with Pause and
     Stop, the same landing into the project. File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) stays the one door.
  3. **Devices**: built-in and USB/UVC cameras and iPhone Continuity Camera; a live preview of
     the chosen camera in the panel; a choice of resolution and frame rate from the camera's
     formats, otherwise its best format.
  4. **Audio**: the chosen microphone (which can be the camera's own) is its own audio file on
     its own track, lined up to the picture, as screen recording does today.

  Everything else recording.md decided carries over: a recording is ordinary media, the files
  live in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, the panel asks for the grants and the tool never
  does, the microphone is a second file, a pause is a sequence of files, one grouped edit lands
  everything, and every door has an MCP mirror (a new source is an argument of `record_screen`,
  the voice-over's precedent, unless a phase records otherwise). Callouts stay out for the
  reason recording.md gives: a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant. **Risk
  accepted:** a second capture stack (`AVCaptureSession` for a camera) beside ScreenCaptureKit,
  a Camera grant and its entitlement, and a camera's own clock to line up with the screen's and
  the microphone's; CR0 measures each before any of it is built.

- **CAM-2 — The camera spike's rule (CR0), fixed before its run.** `tools/proof/camera_spike/`
  measures camera capture alone and beside a running screen recording; `results.json` stores
  this file's SHA-256 as `rule_sha256`, so the rule a recorded run read is pinned. The VERDICT
  line reads `VERDICT writer=<movie-output|asset-writer|STOP> screen_start=<E1|E2|STOP>
  continuity_key=<needed|not-needed|unmeasured> camera_entitlement=<needed|not-needed|unmeasured>
  best_format=<per-device summary>`, or `VERDICT NOT MEASURED: <reason>` when every `write` row
  is skipped.
  - **Writer.** `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` is chosen unless, on the chosen camera at D3's
    format, any run shows one of: (a) frames written < 98 % of span × rate while W3's
    (`AVAssetWriter` fed by an `AVCaptureVideoDataOutput` on W2's whole device configuration)
    are ≥ 98 %; (b) no `startPTS` callback, or no conversion of it to the host clock; (c)
    neither HEVC nor H.264 is writable at that format; (d) P1's median resume start latency
    exceeds P2's by more than one frame interval. Any of these picks `AVAssetWriter`. If
    neither path reaches 98 %, the verdict is STOP.
  - **Screen start.** The truth is the display link's `targetTimestamp` (the presentation host
    time, not the draw time) logged for the counter code read in the screen file's first frame.
    The estimators are E1, the arrival host time of `recordingOutputDidStartRecording`, and E2,
    the PTS of the first `.screen` frame at or after E1. The first of E1, E2 whose |error|
    against that truth is ≤ 16.7 ms in every S run is chosen; if neither passes, the verdict is
    STOP.
  - **Black frame.** A frame whose mean luma (8-bit, 0–255) is < 24.
  - **Continuity key.** `unmeasured` when D1 marks no device `isContinuityCamera`. Otherwise
    `needed` iff D2 without `.continuityCamera` and without the key
    `NSCameraUseContinuityCameraDeviceType` lists no device (matched by `uniqueID`) that D1
    marks `isContinuityCamera`, else `not-needed`.
  - **Camera entitlement.** `unmeasured` when T3 (the hardened copy WITH
    `com.apple.security.device.camera`) delivers no frame or only black frames — a dark room or
    a covered lens measures nothing. Otherwise `needed` iff T2 (the hardened copy without it)
    delivers no frame or only black frames, else `not-needed`.
  - **Best format.** The largest width × height whose maximum rate is ≥ 30; ties go to the
    higher maximum rate, then to the format listed first.

  A skipped row (no grant, no camera, no person) is never a failure; the probe never asks for a
  grant but under `--ask`, which asks for Camera and Microphone only, never Screen Recording.
  **Risk accepted:** a bare binary's grant is its responsible process's (road map 3 R0 q1), so
  T2 and T3 measure the hardened runtime under the terminal's grant, not a signed bundle's own
  prompt; that prompt is a person's check in CR1.

- **CAM-3 — The camera recorder's rules (CR1a), recorded before its code; amends CAM-2's Best

# Spec §11 — decisions: Audio (the owner's audio pass, from 2026-10-30)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The owner's pass over a clip's sound, begun 2026-10-30 to turn a desktop USB microphone's
recording into usable audio for a video. Its IDs are the AU- series. Each was recorded before
its code.

The road map that made AU-2…AU-156 is closed (2026-10-31): its condensed record is
`designs/adr/audio.md`, the original `archive/audio.md` (AP0 the plan and spikes S1–S4, then one
record per phase, in the order they landed), and the survey it came from
`archive/audio-survey.md`.

- **AU-1 — `audio.volume`'s ceiling is ×32 (+30.1 dB), not ×4; the Volume slider keeps its
  0–400 % travel and the field beside it takes the rest (owner, 2026-10-30: "400% should not be
  a hard max").** The owner's recording `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a` (a RØDE USB microphone,
  30.4 s of AAC mono at 48 kHz) peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated loudness of −44.7 LUFS
  (ffmpeg's `volumedetect` and `ebur128`), so Normalize wanted ×7.55 to reach −1 dBFS and stopped
  at ×4, −6.5 dBFS. The ceiling stays — `MAX_GAIN` still bounds `check_audio`'s refusal,
  `clamp_audio` and the envelope, so one bad patch cannot send +80 dB to the mix — but at ×32:
  Normalize now reaches −1 dBFS from a peak as quiet as −31.1 dBFS, and 30 dB covers the gap
  between this microphone's −44.7 LUFS and a −14 LUFS delivery. 32 rather than 31.62 (exactly
  +30 dB) so the refusal reads a whole number: "audio.volume must be between 0 and 32".
  - Measured before the change: AVFoundation's audio mix applies a `setVolumeRamp` volume above
    4 exactly. The recording read through `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` in 32-bit float peaks at
    4.000, 7.600, 16.000, 32.000 and 64.000 times its ×1 peak at those volumes (a scratch probe
    of 2026-10-30), so ×4 was the model's rule and nothing beneath it changes.
  - The Volume row: the slider keeps 0–400 %, where its resolution is useful (a 0–3200 % rail
    would put 100 % at a thirty-second of its width); the field takes 0–3200 %. A value above
    400 % pins the knob at the rail's end, and a drag writes the rail's own range. The quick
    picks are unchanged.
  - One Swift copy of the ceiling, `AudioNormalize.maxGain`, which the Volume row's field and
    the agent's sentences now read too, is held to the core's refusal by `core/tests/audio_gain.rs`,
    reading its `static let` line as `graphic_ffi.rs` reads `maxTextureSide`. No `rc_*` export:
    `ReelCore.swift` is over its cap, and one constant does not need the FFI.
  - No format bump. The file's shape is unchanged and the reader runs no range check
    (`Project::validate` does not call `check_audio`), so an older build opens a project with a
    volume above 4, plays it at ×4 through `audio.rs`'s clamp and writes the stored number back
    unchanged. A bump guards against a loss on that round trip, and there is none.
  - What it accepts: a mix can go further past full scale than before. The preview's output and
    an un-normalised export clip there (phase 5d's 16-bit decode, which says so); a normalised
    export gains in float (#86) and does not. Normalize itself still lands at −1 dBFS.

AU-2…AU-4 open road map "audio" (`archive/audio.md`, from `archive/audio-survey.md`'s tiers A
and B), recorded at its AP0 from the owner's answers of 2026-10-30 to the road map's five
choices ("Yes, lift scopes, and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the
rest), before any of its code. **Numbering from here:** each phase records its decisions in a
block of its own, APn's as AU-n0…AU-n9 (AP1's AU-10…, AP10's AU-100…), so phases built in
parallel lanes never claim one ID; AP0's are AU-2…AU-9.

- **AU-2 — Audio beyond what shipped is in scope: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
  built-in audio units (owner, 2026-10-30, choice 1; amends spec §1).** Spec §1's non-goal
  "audio beyond what shipped … so no EQ, mix buses or Audio Units, while offline voice effects
  are deferred rather than out" is lifted. In: Frame Job's own DSP stages, track and master
  processing, and the audio units macOS itself ships (`AUSoundIsolation`, `AVAudioUnitEQ`, the
  dynamics and time-pitch units), run in the process as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for
  speed-ramp audio. Out, under §1's plugin system: hosting third-party Audio Unit plug-ins (the
  survey's C5). Tier C of the survey is not in the road map; it is neither in nor out until the
  owner asks.
- **AU-3 — Live stages are Frame Job's own DSP in the tap, in one fixed order; Apple's units
  only where Frame Job cannot write its own (owner, 2026-10-30, choices 4 and 5).** EQ and the
  high-pass, the hum notch, the gate/expander, the de-esser and the limiter are written beside
  the compressor: real-time safe in the `MTAudioProcessingTap`, deterministic, and proved
  against analytic responses. Apple's units are used for ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`)
  and E8's voice effects, both rendered offline per clip window into `cache/` on the speed-ramp
  audio pattern. AP0's spike S1 may overturn the first half by measurement, recorded as an
  amendment here. The clip chain's order is fixed: channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch →
  isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, then the fader (the
  core's envelope). Every stage is off by default and inert when off, so a project that uses
  none plays and exports byte-identical to today (a track whose clips ask for nothing still
  gets no tap). A closed vocabulary, as R5-1 has every effect: no user-ordered chain, no
  per-clip stage list.
- **AU-4 — Normalize targets loudness: −16 LUFS by default at −1 dBTP, Peak kept beside it
  (owner, 2026-10-30, choices 2 and 3).** AP1 adds Normalize's Loudness mode (a target in
  LUFS, gated BS.1770 over the window that plays) beside today's Peak; the button stays Peak
  until AP2's limiter can hold −1 dBTP, and from AP2 its default is Loudness. The default
  target is −16 LUFS integrated, with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128)
  as quick picks; the ceiling is −1 dBTP. `normalize_clip` keeps `peak_db` and gains the
  loudness mode's arguments.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Screen recording (road map 3)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

- **Screen recording is IN; camera recording and callouts stay OUT** (road
  map 3, reversing §1's day-one non-goal). A screen recording is the input
  the whole product was shaped around; camera capture is a second capture
  stack and callouts are a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant.
  What ScreenCaptureKit draws into the pixels for free — the cursor, and
  a ring around each click — is taken; nothing is reconstructed afterwards.
  **Amended by CAM-1** (camera recording, CR0): camera recording is now IN
  — a camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and
  track, through this recorder's panel (`camera-recording.md`); callouts
  stay OUT.
- **A recording is ordinary media.** The recorder writes a file and the app
  imports it through exactly the path File ▸ Open and Add Media… use
  (`adoptImported`, the two-try placement). The model learns nothing: no
  source kind, no flag, no schema bump. Every op, cache and export treats a
  recording clip as the media clip it is.
- **The file lives in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`**, named by date and
  time, never in the package and never in the temporary directory: an
  untitled document has no package (§5.6), and a recording is ORIGINAL
  footage, so the one place it may not go is where a cache is regenerable.
  Consolidate carries it in on the same terms as any other file.
  `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides the folder for a proof.
  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0): `~/Movies/Reelcut Recordings/` is now
  `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`.
- **The canvas takes the recorder's RATE; the media record takes the
  file's.** ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when the screen changes,
  so its files are variable-rate and the probe honestly reports something
  like 24981/1000 (measured); the untitled document is built at the 30 or
  60 the panel asked for, because that is the grid the person chose, and
  `set_canvas` is NOT used for it afterwards — an untitled document's
  first project is not an undo step, and the rate is part of what the
  document IS.
- **The panel asks for the grants; the tool never does.** `Transcriber`'s
  rule for two grants: Screen Recording (`CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`
  reads, `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` asks) and Microphone
  (`AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus`, `requestAccess`). The microphone
  status is read BEFORE any `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is constructed, because
  that initializer prompts on its own. `record_screen` reads and refuses by
  name with the fix in the sentence. The built app needs BOTH the plist
  usage key and the hardened-runtime entitlement
  `com.apple.security.device.audio-input` for the microphone; Screen
  Recording needs neither.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it

  core's `[clip tick, source tick]` pairs, and the ONE place Swift reads
  between them (linearly, as the ramp renderer plays them; no rate computed
  here, D2-1). Checked ONCE on decode, read by BINARY SEARCH both ways
  (`source(atClip:)`, `clip(atSource:)`), because a ramp holds a point every
  600 ticks and the waveform and the silence walk read per column and per
  bucket; `SourceMaps` is how a reader is handed the maps of its snapshot's
  handle. A reader takes the map only when it is `ramped`, so a constant
  clip keeps today's arithmetic exactly. `rate` is the core's rate profile
  (`RatePoint`s, SR-26), checked on decode; a list that fails the check is
  [] and the map is kept. `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` is
  the filmstrip's and the waveform's map-aware `sourceTime`
  (`TimelineView.swift` is frozen; it holds only `sourceMaps`, set in
  `refreshTimeline` from the same handle as the snapshot).
- `DuckSpeech.swift` — Duck by Speech's Swift half (spec §11 AU-110, AU-111,
  AU-113): `spans` (VAD probabilities → source-tick spans: p ≥
  `defaultVoiceConfidence`, gaps under 0.2 s bridged, ends clamped to the
  media's duration), `ops` (the `set_media_speech` each media without spans
  needs, or a `Refusal` naming the clip or the file), `problem` (the same
  answer without reading a cache, for the popup), and `DuckCurves` (one
  handle's plan `ducks`, decoded lazily once, for the timeline). Every duck
  edit of a Speech duck, in the Ducking section and over `set_audio`, puts
  `ops` before the `set_audio`. No span→time or gain arithmetic: that is
  the core's.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the

  (spec §11 #337): exactly round(range × 48 000) frames, the crossing buffer
  cut, later buffers read and dropped, a short read padded with silence at
  the master's depth; the measurement feeds the same count. The alpha movie rows' frames (`prores_4444`,
  `hevc_alpha`) are straightened in the video pump before `retimed`:
  un-premultiplied, each transparent pixel within 4 px of a visible one
  filled with the nearest one's colour, and labelled `StraightAlpha`, with
  `hevc_alpha`'s encoder key straight too (`ExportStraightAlpha.swift`, spec
  §11 G-35): `prores_4444`'s in place in float, `hevc_alpha`'s rounded first
  into a pooled 32BGRA buffer (`ExportFrames`, `ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`,
  PR-3); the fill is one generic pass over `StraightAlphaLayout` (`BGRA8`,
  `RGBAHalf`), whose `allVisible` keeps the whole-row check vectorised.
  `h264`'s and `hevc`'s frames are rounded to 8 bits the same way and not
  straightened, and `hevc` is pinned to Main; `hevc_10bit` maps to `.hevc`
  too, is told apart by its codec name (`isMain10`), is pinned to Main 10
  and, like every other row, gets the frame as drawn.
  `ExportWriter` FILLS the frame when a fit would leave at most
  a pixel uncovered, or — the frame a canvas-SHAPED size less at most one
  pixel on each axis, `(bw + a)·ch == (bh + b)·cw` for some `a`, `b` in
  {0, 1}, at any scale — when a fill would overshoot by at most one
  (`shapeGap`: `gap <= limit`, in integers), and letterboxes past that, where
  an alpha-carrying movie row (`prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`) is refused instead
  (padding inverts the alpha; a pure scale is fine); so no size of the
  canvas's own shape is refused for being odd, and a typed size of another
  shape is judged as the even frame it becomes; the frame is the size the
  CORE resolved, already even where the row needs it (spec §11 G-33), and
  `encodedSize` is only the floor under it; a missing encoder is
  `.presetUnavailable` and no file (`Exporter.encoderOutcome`, in
  `ExporterErrors.swift`, applied where `startWriting` hears the pipeline); `apng` FITS instead and must not
  grow the guard. GIF and APNG refuse past 600 frames rather than truncate.
  `renderFrame` is documented off-main. Audio export is NOT bit-deterministic
  within an 8 ms window at a duck ramp edge (AVFoundation's mix); a duck-free
  project decodes byte-identical. `ExportError` is `ExporterErrors.swift`'s.
  An export PINS the `GraphicSet` it was handed for its whole life, GATES it
  before the build (`ExporterGraphics.graphicsRefusal`: a graphic clip in
  the range, or in any nest reached from one, however deep, whose module did
  not compile or is missing, refuses before the destination is touched), and
  ABORTS on a recorded failure: `pollProgress` cancels and `finish` removes
  the file and answers `.graphicFailed`, whatever the pipeline said.
  `startWriting` starts the graphic prefetch (`startGraphicPrefetch`, G-26)

  `Exporter.graphicWarnings` (`ExporterGraphics.swift`'s
