governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11

  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s

  partner through `edit_link.rs`'s closures. `whole_media_length`,
  `edit_clip_timing.rs`'s `trim_end` and `set_speed` hold a media clip's window INSIDE its file, each
  through `source_window.rs`'s one bound, so
  `in + duration × speed ≤ media.duration` and the plan's segment rate is
  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,
  `edit_nest.rs`'s `unnest` and `edit_background.rs`'s timed plate. Over
  the cap, known debt (below).
- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,
  their speed bounds and clip-relative action rescaling; `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`
  (×12, spec §11 #190) and `speed_limits`, which `rc_speed_limits` publishes;
  `set_speed` takes a `rate` or a `duration` (Fit to duration), exactly one.
  On a ramped clip (SR-19 (a), (b)) both rate edits scale the WHOLE profile
  by one factor (`profile_factors`, None on every constant clip):
  `scaled_profile` scales the base, every end rate and every speed span
  (`scaled_span`, snapped, never clamped, which `rescale_actions` also uses),
  writes an unclamped rate as asked, holds the window, then re-clamps the
  other actions into the held duration through `resnap_actions`.
  `trim_start` advances a graphic's `in` through `graphic_advanced` (no speed,
  no head bound, saturating at 0); `trim_end` leaves `length` alone.
- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and
  audio halves; a pure move out of `edit_clip.rs` (grading L3).
- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized
  footage and honours `canvas.fit_new_clips`; Fill is a REQUIREMENT, ignores
  it, scales up as readily as down and clamps to `SCALE_MAX`); a pure move
  out of `edit_clip.rs` (road map "audio" AP9's toll).
- `edit_link.rs` — linked pairs (format 28, spec §11 AU-90…AU-96): Detach
  Audio's picture and sound name each other in `Clip.linked`. `partner`
  (mutual, one container); `with_links` (the named clips, then each one's
  partner on an UNLOCKED track — `move_clips`, `split_clips`,
  `duplicate_clips`, `nest_clips`, `ripple_delete`) and `delete_closure` (a
  linked sound half named alone goes alone); `settle_links`, which `finish`
  runs BEFORE its identity comparison so no op stores a one-sided link and
  none clears the half it orphaned, and `check_links`, `validate`'s refusal
  of one; `pair_split_halves` and `relink_copies` (`duplicate`, `paste` top
  level and nests, `unnest`); `carried_edge` (`trim_start`, `trim_end`,
  `roll`: the partner whose same edge coincided follows unless `alone`);
  `linked_rate_refusal` (speed, direction and speed-naming actions refused);
  and the one op, `attach_audio`. The shift's half is `edit_time.rs`'s
  `shifted`.
- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve
  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions
  check caller-allocated candidates against the input project; both write
  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on
  exactly the chosen tracks before `finish`. `finish` remains equality first,
  validation second, and does not itself refuse. `Clip::placed` is the one
  literal of a newly placed clip (each placing site overrides it by struct
  update); `add_tracks_behind` and `Landing` are unnest's and paste's shared
  landing: deficit tracks inserted behind, fallbacks pushed in front, the
  touched tracks in first-seen order for `finish_placement`.
- `edit_split.rs` — `split_clip` and what the SECOND clip inherits: base
  props from the evaluation at the cut, unfinished actions rebased, a
  straddled one narrowed, presets and motion halves anchored to the two
  ends. Every splitter in the crate routes here, so a rule stated once is a
  rule they all obey. A free function over `&mut Project` because it is
  called mid-edit on a clone the caller is still assembling.
  A graphic's second half gets `in + cut` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_advanced`, and BOTH halves' `length` are pinned to the ORIGINAL's
  `effective_length` (G-9), so every splitter obeys it, and its `props` the
  evaluated ones, a straddled action's first half ending at them (G-34).
- `edit_props.rs` — the five patches (`set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`,
  `set_shape`, `set_clip`), `Project::settle_video` (the one chain that
  makes a video group storable — empty motion → null, `check_video`,
  identity curves dropped, `check_blend` / `check_adjustment_video` /
  `check_qualifier_clip` / `check_look_media`, `snap_motion` — run by
  `set_video` and by every pasted video group) and
  `normalise_and_check_group` beside it (`settle_video` for a video group,
  the range check for the other three) (the one NORMALISATION a copied
  group needs first: a clipboard payload is a third door for a `Motion`, and
  an empty one has two spellings; only the file reader does not normalise;
  the copied group is checked before its present video/text timing is
  snapped), and `normalise_and_check_pasted`, which runs it over every group
  of every clip `paste` lands — nested ones in a second pass, once every
  copy is in — naming the PAYLOAD's clip id (`pasted clip N: …`, issue #62),
  `check_blend`, the one check about a CLIP rather than a value (a nest clip
  cannot blend), and `snap_motion` / `snap_animation`, which put the ticks a
  patch or checked copied group carries on the frame grid AFTER the range
  check, so a refusal names what the caller sent. What a patch may CARRY is
  `patch.rs`'s and nothing here restates it.
- `patch.rs` — reading a caller-authored patch, cut out of `edit_props.rs`
  under the size rule: `Group` — the four PATCH groups; `paste_attributes` takes these four and
  `graphic` as `edit_paste_attributes.rs`'s `PasteGroup`, and a patch has no
  fifth group — and its per-group template, `check_keys` (the
  walk of keys and JSON kinds, array indices in the path) and `merge_group`
  (the one read of a group patch — the walk, the deep merge and the
  path-tracking deserialise — the new text and shape clips' patches
  included), so every refusal names the path, indices included, and the
  value. `check_group_patch` is the same walk and read for a group that is
  NOT being merged into a stored one (an action's end state), and
  `unknown_key` is that refusal's one spelling. A patch merges key by key at
  every depth, an array replaces its list, and `null` clears an optional key
  (a required one refuses it). `COMPLETE_ENTRIES` is the one exception to
  "absent keeps": a `video.filters` entry must name both its keys, because a
  list replaces whole and the type's defaults would invent a filter. Nothing
  here is handed a clip or a project: what a patch may carry is a fact about
  the vocabulary, which is `props_check.rs`'s reason for existing one step
  further on. `GROUPS` — every group in its order on `Clip`, the order
  `paste` and a default `paste_attributes` visit them — lives here, its one
  home. The audio template holds format 29's keys, format 31's
  `isolation` and format 32's `eq` (every slot, `bypass` true), `hum` and
  `channels` (`swapped`) at NON-default values,
  since a default is no longer written and the key check reads the template.
- `props_check.rs` — the range checks every value written into a property
  group passes first (`check_video` / `check_audio` / `check_text` /
  `check_shape`, the `finite` / `in_range` family, the bounds `actions_clamp.rs`'s `clamp_video` reads too). A range check is a fact about the vocabulary,
  not about an edit — and it runs BEFORE `edit_props.rs` snaps a patch's
  ticks, which is what lets a refusal name the number the caller sent rather
  than the one a snap rounded it to. Gradient stops are deliberately NOT
  order-checked: a refusal would break dragging one stop past another
  mid-gesture, so the renderer sorts, and the comment says so where the
  check would have gone. A list entry's key names its index —
  `video.filters[0].amount`, `video.obscure[1].x`,
  `shape.gradient.stops[0].color` — so a refusal names the entry as well as
  the field (issue #89).
- `grade_check.rs` — tier 2's range checks (spec §11 GR-11), called from `check_video`: each
  wheel's x, y and master −1…1, and x² + y² ≤ 1 (to `WHEEL_RIM_TOLERANCE`, 1e-9, so a rim point
  is never refused) refused in its own sentence; `actions_clamp.rs`'s `clamp_wheels` closes an
  action's end. `check_curves` (GR-12): 2–16 points, x and y 0…1, x strictly rising, each in
  its own sentence, a hue curve's x 0 ≤ x < 360 and its value in its domain (GR-32);
  `clamp_curves` closes an action's end per domain. `check_qualifier` (GR-13): each
  bound in its own sentence, low ≤ high, then `blur` 0…1 last (GR-35); `clamp_qualifier`
  closes an action's end (a non-finite blur to 0, then 0…1);
  `edit_adjustment.rs`'s `check_qualifier_clip` refuses one on any other clip.
- `edit_track.rs` — tracks, markers and the media list: the three lists a
  clip sits in. The canvas left here at road map 7's D2·3 toll. `clip_list`
  is the ONE spelling of the clips a `with_clips` refusal names — three ids
  and then a count, so a media used by two hundred clips still answers a
  sentence a caller can read — shared by `remove_track` and `remove_media`. It
  keeps `MEDIA_KEYS` and `check_media_fields` (the post-schema checks a media
  record passes, in one order and one set of sentences), which
  `edit_relink.rs` reads for a relink's probe and `edit_paste.rs` (after
  `normalize_original`) for a pasted row it appends; `relink_media` moved to
  `edit_relink.rs`.
- `edit_relink.rs` — `relink_media` (spec §11 #63): points a media at another
  file and, given the new file's `probe` (the host's `MediaImporter.probe`
  descriptor minus `path` and `bookmark`), takes its duration, size, rate and
  flags, refuses a file of another kind in its own sentence, and holds every
  `media`-source clip of it, on the timeline and in every stored nest, whose
  duration runs past the new file's window to `source_window.rs`'s
  `duration_resnapped`. A probe's `original` replaces the stored one (none
  clears it), and a probe rewrites the media's `speech` in the same edit
  (spans at or past the new duration dropped, ends clamped to it, cleared
  when the list empties or the file has no audio; spec §11 AU-116), so a
  relink never fails `validate` over spans. No probe keeps the record
  (Consolidate, the open-time re-anchor).
- `media_speech.rs` — a media's speech spans (format 29, spec §11 AU-110):
  `set_media_speech` (an identity on equal spans) and `check_media_speech`
  (audio, each span inside the file, sorted, not overlapping, at most
  `MAX_SPEECH_SPANS` 100,000, each its own sentence; `validate` calls it
  too).
- `edit_canvas.rs` — the document's own shape: `set_canvas` and the three
  things it does to the rest of the document — `check_dimension` (a
  dimension is even, because H.264 encodes in macroblocks), `rescale` (a
  size change moves every clip's `x`, `y` and `scale`, each axis by its own
  ratio and `scale` by the smaller of the two) and `resnap` (a rate change
  normalizes top-level and each stored nest's clip times through `frame_grid.rs`
  and drops the second of two top-level markers a coarser grid lands on one tick).
- `edit_time.rs` — ripple, insert time, `ripple_delete_ranges` (the pairs are
  ordered, MERGED — touching as well as overlapping — then cut and closed
  right to left as ONE edit; the singular delegates to it), `lift_range`
  (the hole left open), `close_gap` (refuses rather than closing part way, and
  refuses naming what is there when `at` is on a clip or nothing follows it,
  spec §11 #88),
  freeze frame, `shift_clips`, `shifted` (what a shift moves: every unlocked
  clip at or after the boundary and each one's linked partner;
  `shift_clips` moves exactly that set and answers a refusal, nothing moved,
  when a partner would start before 0), and `locked_track` — THE locked-track
  refusal's sentence, written once here for its three callers
  (`close_gap`, `edit_insert.rs`'s `insert_clip`, `edit_transition.rs`'s
  rippled form), each passing the clause after the comma.
- `edit_edge.rs` · `edit_insert.rs` — the cutting moves that keep something
  fixed on purpose: `slip` and `roll` (a `still` slips the frame it holds;
  any other non-media source is an `Err`; roll's predecessor must end
  EXACTLY at the clip's start); `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip`,
  compositions of split + insert time + add made ONE op so a drop is one
  undo step and carries the rule neither half states — an insert cuts only
  the destination track (and a cut clip's linked partner, AU-92) and then
  shifts every unlocked one.
  `roll` is a front trim on its clip, so it advances `graphic.in` as
  `trim_start` does; the predecessor's end is an end trim and keeps `length`.
- `edit_transition.rs` — the WRITE half of a transition: `set_transition`,
  `set_transition_duration`, `set_gained_transitions` (a clip that gains an
  overlap gains a transition) and `add_transition` (an overlap built from
  the two clips' handles at a hard cut). `transition.rs` is the READ half and
  nothing here restates it. `transition_too_short`, THE too-short sentence both forms of
  `add_transition` share (spec §11 #88); `set_transition_duration` refuses on
  a track's first clip and past the pair's snapped overlap limit, naming it
  (#88, #175).
- `edit_transition_shift.rs` — `add_transition_by_shift`, the `ripple` half
  of `add_transition`: the same overlap made by sliding the incoming clip
  and everything at or after the cut left through `shift_clips`. Cut out of
  `edit_transition.rs` under the size rule (the E1 reader review's toll T),
  a pure move: the handle form spends unused SOURCE and moves nothing,
  this one spends the TIMELINE and moves `close_gap`'s set by `close_gap`'s
  rules. The request is counted in whole frames of the real grid
  (`time::frames_in`) and the incoming clip lands on it (`time::frames_back`);
  a request under one grid frame refuses in `transition_too_short`'s words,
  right after the lock check.
- `edit_transition_style.rs` — `set_transition_style`: a transition's curve,
  whether it crossfades the sound and (format 29, spec §11 AU-115) the
  crossfade's `audio_shape`, its kind untouched. Cut out of
  `edit_transition.rs` under the size rule (road map "audio" AP11's toll, a
  pure move).
- `edit_action.rs` · `edit_nest.rs` · `edit_paste.rs` — the action ops and
  their no-overlap rule, plus `check_end_patch`, the END patch's door: the
  three groups §5.4 allows (a `shape` is an unknown key), a `null` that
  REMOVES at every depth rather than clearing, and `patch.rs`'s walk and
  read per group. The door is composed here because which groups an end
  patch names, and what a `null` in one means, are facts about an ACTION;
  values are deliberately not range-checked, except a graphic prop's end
  (G-34 (c), `edit_action_graphic.rs`), and `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_video` is the last line of defence for them. `set_action_end`'s
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14) is the one way to STORE a `null` — the optional
  property keyed OFF at the end — written after the merge and the prune; its
  paths are `group.key`, and `audio.eq.<slot>` (one of `EQ_SLOTS`, AU-88)
  is the only three-part one; `check_off` refuses what `patch` refuses (`not_a_target`'s two sentences,
  and `merge_group`'s read of a `null` for an unknown or a required key),
  and a non-object group slot is replaced by `{}`, never indexed. `set_action`
  refuses `action_past_end` only when the new end is past the clip's end AND
  later than the action's current end (SR-22, #338), so a value-only edit of
  an action a trim left past the end goes through. `nest` and `unnest`
  (fresh ids, content byte-equal; the nest clip on the front-most non-matte
  track, a matte carried only above the copy of its target, unnest aligned on
  the front-most non-matte track — spec §11 MT-5);
  `paste`, whose payload schema is its module doc; `Payload` and
  `parse_payload` are `pub(crate)`, because `edit_paste_attributes.rs` reads
  the same payload.
  `graphic` in a `patch` is `edit_action_graphic.rs`'s arm, read against
  the op's `schema` after the three groups' walk (G-34); in an `off` path it
  is an `Err`.
- `speed_map.rs` — a media clip's SPEED MAP (speed ramps SR-10): the
  clip-time → source-time function its speed actions make (the ease
  integrals of `actions.rs`'s curves), `is_ramped` (media clips only),
  `end_speed`'s clamp, `peak_rate` (the greatest rate the clip NAMES, its
  base and every end rate, the ×12 figure, SR-19 (d)), `source_at`, `rate_at`,
  `rate_in_force` (what `clip_state`'s top-level `speed` answers, SR-21); `of_length` (the
  map over any horizon, reading on past the clip's end with its own
  actions, SR-18 (a)), `time_for_source` (its inverse) and `head_end_rate`
  (a split's straddled head re-solved so both halves meet at S(cut),
  SR-18 (e)); what `content_length_in_source` reads for a ramped clip;
  `rate_profile` (the rate over clip time for the lane's rate line: piece
  edges, and `RATE_SAMPLES` + 1 samples across a ramp piece, SR-26).
- `speed_segments.rs` — the map cut into plan pieces: `Held` at one rate
  (an equal-rate action is held), `Ramp` one video segment per canvas
  frame, and the ramp audio map with a breakpoint every 600 ticks;
  `constant_ramp_audio` is the two-point map, flagged `constant`, that
  `evaluate.rs` puts on a constant Keep pitch off time-scaled audio segment
  so Swift renders it as a ramp's (SR-28).
  `Project::source_map` (SR-20) answers a media clip's source map: a ramped
  clip its ramp audio map, byte-equal to the plan segment's `ramp.map`, a
  constant clip its two points, flagged `ramped` as `is_ramped` is; a
  ramped clip's answer also carries `rate`, `rate_profile`'s list (SR-26),
  and a constant clip's has no `rate` key.
- `edit_action_speed.rs` — `set_action_end`'s speed arm and the overrun
  refusals R1/R2/R3 for `set_action_end`, `set_action` and
  `remove_action`: a ramp that would read past the media's end is refused,
  naming the largest end rate that fits (floored to 0.001,
  `largest_fitting_end_rate`, which split's eased tail also uses, over the
  shared `largest_fitting_rate` that `add_speed_ramp` also solves through).
- `edit_action_ramp.rs` — `add_speed_ramp`, the ramp presets (SR-23, #340):
  Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Speed Dip or Speed Burst as ordinary Speed actions in
  one step, in clip time over `[from, to)` or the whole clip, from the BASE
  `rate_in_force` at `from`; Up and Burst need a rate above it, Down and Dip
  one below. An action anywhere in the span (a dip's hold gap included) is
  refused by name, never replaced, and a preset that would read past the
  media's end is refused naming the rate that fits.
- `edit_action_graphic.rs` — `set_action_end`'s graphic arm (G-34):
  `read_graphic_end` checks the patch's `graphic.props` (never the stored
  end's) against the op's `schema` through `check_typed` under
  `graphic.props.<key>`, discards a `kinds`, refuses a prop its module
  marks `animate: false` (G-41), an undeclared prop, a layer key and a
  missing schema by name (an asset is an ordinary switch, `""` naming no
  image, G-42), and answers each prop's kind and the default for each the
  clip lacks (`schema_default`; an asset's is its string default or `""`); `write_graphic_end` stores `props` and `kinds` by

- `edit_paste_attributes.rs` — `paste_attributes`, cut out of `edit_paste.rs`
  under the size rule as a pure move ahead of spec §11 G-32: the payload's
  EARLIEST clip's property groups (then the front-most, then the lower id —
  never the array's first) copied onto each target, replaced whole and never
  merged. `PasteGroup` is the five names it takes — the four patch groups and
  `graphic`, which is never in the default set: a graphic's `props` copied
  whole onto clips drawn by the SAME module, the target keeping its name,
  size, `in` and `length`, written with `insert` and `shift_remove`
  (`model_graphic.rs`'s rule). A target key the payload lacks that an
  action on the target names (`names_prop`) is kept (G-34 (d), amending
  G-32 (e)). `skip_missing` drops a named group the payload
  clip lacks and skips a target that cannot take one. **The copied props are
  shape-checked once, the first time a target takes them**: a paste nothing
  takes never reads the map. `patch::Group` gains no variant for it.
- `edit_zoom.rs` — `add_zoom_action`, the screencast zoom, and `ZoomRegion`,
  the one op ARGUMENT that is a caller-authored object: its `Deserialize` is
  written out rather than derived so it answers as a patch does — an object
  required (a list is not read member by member), an unknown or missing
  member named, a wrong-typed one named by its path. **Its module doc
  IS the placement equation** between the region frame and canvas pixels,
  rotation and crop included; it composes `add_action` + `set_action` +
  `set_action_end` so a drag is one undo step and every refusal is inherited.
- `edit_adjustment.rs` — `Source::Adjustment`'s rules (spec §11 GR-6):
  `add_adjustment_clip`, and the refusals every other door asks it for — a
  transition (from `add_transition`, `set_transition`, `set_transition_style`
  and the overlap rule), a nest, and the blur, sharpen and pixelate filters
  and any blend mode. The recipe draws it as `{"kind":"adjustment"}` (plus its `qualifier` when
  it has one and `selection: true` when `RecipeOptions.selection` names it, GR-13); and on a
  matte track it is dropped before the frame's mattes (inert).
- `edit_background.rs` — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`: one
  clip on a NEW back-most track, OPS rather than app-side composites because
  the composite carries constraints no half states. A blurred copy drops
  `enabled.audio`, `audio.duck`, the transition, the actions and the label
  (each a wrong picture or a wrong sound if carried) and refuses a nest.
  Default plate colour is white: the canvas is already black.
- `actions.rs` — action evaluation and interpolation, and `clip_state`
  (with a top-level `speed`, `speed_map.rs`'s rate in force, the inspector's
  Rate inside an action, SR-21);
  `video_json` / `color_json` write all thirteen colour keys, the tone keys at
  0 included, for the five callers that must see them (the base state,
  `clip_state`, `patch.rs`'s template, `recipe_layer.rs`, `edit_split.rs`);
  its last line of defence is `actions_clamp.rs`'s, and a graphic's props
  are `actions_graphic.rs`'s (spec §11 G-34), carried in `Evaluated.graphic`
  and `clip_state`'s `graphic`. **The LIST rule is stated here once as the
  crate's**: an end patch interpolates a list per index when the lengths
  match and each pair of entries agrees on its discrete fields (`kind`,
  `shape`), and switches at the end otherwise; `video.filters` and `video.obscure` are both governed by it and carry no code of their own.
- `actions_clamp.rs` — `clamp_video`, `clamp_audio` and `clamp_text`, the
  evaluator's last line of defence (`set_action_end` checks a `video`,
  `audio` or `text` end patch's keys and kinds but deliberately not its
  VALUES, and never looks at the clip for them; this bounds every value
  such a patch can carry and forces `normal` on a nest clip), with
  `bounded` / `finite_or`; the first two a pure move out of `actions.rs`
  (issue batch B87, toll A), `clamp_text` added by #353.
- `actions_curves.rs` — `curves_json` (all six curves, an absent one
  as its domain's identity, for `video_json`'s callers),
  `align_identity_curves` (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32: an identity curve
  meeting a curve of another count in an action takes that curve's x's,
  its ends at 0 and 1 on a tone curve and every value the neutral on a
  hue curve, so a grade animates from neutral), and `CurveBlend`,
  `curve_blends` and `blended_curves_json` (spec §11 GR-34: two
  non-identity curves of different counts in an action blend their
  values — the evaluator names each such channel with its clamped end
  curve and the eased t in `Evaluated.curve_blends`, and only the recipe
  layer and `clip_state` write it, as `{from, to, t}`; never a file).
- `actions_qualifier.rs` — `qualifier_json` (spec §11 GR-35): a qualifier
  with its `blur` present even at 0, which `actions.rs`'s `video_json` writes
  for a non-neutral one so the blur animates from 0; and `align_hue_center`
  (spec §11 GR-13): before
  the lerp, an action's target hue centre moves by ±360 when the two
  centres are more than 180° apart, so the centre animates the short
  way round (350 → 10 through 0); `clamp_qualifier` brings it back
  into [0, 360).
- `actions_audio.rs` — the audio group's two evaluation rules (road map
  "audio" AP8b, spec §11 AU-86): `audio_json` writes the group with
  `isolation` present even at 0, which `actions.rs` uses for the base state
  so an action toward an Amount ramps from 0; and `HELD_AUDIO_NUMBERS` (the
  EQ's two slopes, the hum's mains and harmonics, and the leveller's
  `response`, each response its own curve, AU-66 (f)) with `hold_audio_steps`,
  after the spanning action's `lerp`, holding each at its start value until
  the action's end.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).

  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,

  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s

  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence

  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /

  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`

- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`

  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s

- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11

  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one

  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`

  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in

  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps
  present base motion/text timing through the patch snappers, and snaps a
  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))
  `resnap_actions` snaps the speed actions without clamping them into the
  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds
  the duration a second time over the snapped map.
- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.
  **Every name here carries its UNIT**, because the readers divide by a
  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in
  TIMELINE ticks. **Every site that WRITES a media clip's window reads the
  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
  and `duration_at_speed` what
  `set_speed` writes. No local clamp anywhere else. A measurement is a
  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle
  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one
  `round(Δ × speed)` mover the six placement sites used to write out. Cut
  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.
- `time.rs` — `Ticks`, `TIMESCALE`, `Fps`, frame snapping, timecode
  format/parse (non-drop `HH:MM:SS:FF` and `HH:MM:SS.mmm`). Snapping keeps
  frame indices wide through directional adjustment and saturates only at the
  public tick/index result. `frames_in` (whole grid frames in a length),
  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position
  that stay within a span), `frames_between` (the whole grid frames between
  two positions) and `one_frame` (the grid's own first frame, which
  `Project::frame` is at every rate, 1/30 s only at a degenerate rate; spec
  §11 #174) count on the canvas's own grid at a rate the
  timescale does not divide (spec §11 #42).
- `time_bounds.rs` — the single structural-time admission checker and
  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,
  clips, source positions and actions, including clip/action endpoints in
  i128. `Project::validate` and `format::write` both call it; vocabulary
  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-four op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (twenty-three kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.
- `scope.rs` — editing INSIDE a nest: the envelope's `scope` key. Builds a
  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.
- `edit_graphic.rs` — `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`: every argument
  checked through `model_graphic.rs` BEFORE `edit_clip.rs`'s
  `add_described_clip` (`pub(crate)`, with `Described`) places the clip, so
  the op table's bound probe reaches the side check on any project;
  `set_graphic`'s patch reader takes `name`, `width`, `height`, `length`,
  `props` and refuses `in` by name. With a `schema`, a `null` for a prop
  an action on the clip names stores the schema's default (G-34 (d)).
- `edit_clip.rs` — clip construction and placement callers: `add_clip`, move,

  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,
  `edit_nest.rs`'s `unnest` and `edit_background.rs`'s timed plate. Over

- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,

  `set_speed` takes a `rate` or a `duration` (Fit to duration), exactly one.
  On a ramped clip (SR-19 (a), (b)) both rate edits scale the WHOLE profile

- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and

- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized

  (mutual, one container); `with_links` (the named clips, then each one's
  partner on an UNLOCKED track — `move_clips`, `split_clips`,

- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve
  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions
  check caller-allocated candidates against the input project; both write
  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on
  exactly the chosen tracks before `finish`. `finish` remains equality first,
  validation second, and does not itself refuse. `Clip::placed` is the one
  literal of a newly placed clip (each placing site overrides it by struct

- `edit_split.rs` — `split_clip` and what the SECOND clip inherits: base
  props from the evaluation at the cut, unfinished actions rebased, a
  straddled one narrowed, presets and motion halves anchored to the two
  ends. Every splitter in the crate routes here, so a rule stated once is a
  rule they all obey. A free function over `&mut Project` because it is
  called mid-edit on a clone the caller is still assembling.
  A graphic's second half gets `in + cut` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s

- `edit_props.rs` — the five patches (`set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`,

  makes a video group storable — empty motion → null, `check_video`,
  identity curves dropped, `check_blend` / `check_adjustment_video` /
  `check_qualifier_clip` / `check_look_media`, `snap_motion` — run by

  `normalise_and_check_group` beside it (`settle_video` for a video group,

  patch or checked copied group carries on the frame grid AFTER the range

  `patch.rs`'s and nothing here restates it.
- `patch.rs` — reading a caller-authored patch, cut out of `edit_props.rs`

  walk of keys and JSON kinds, array indices in the path) and `merge_group`

  "absent keeps": a `video.filters` entry must name both its keys, because a

  here is handed a clip or a project: what a patch may carry is a fact about
  the vocabulary, which is `props_check.rs`'s reason for existing one step
  further on. `GROUPS` — every group in its order on `Clip`, the order

  `isolation` and format 32's `eq` (every slot, `bypass` true), `hum` and

  than the one a snap rounded it to. Gradient stops are deliberately NOT

  **`tiny_http` 0.12's `Server` drop unlinks its path unconditionally (MC1's
  S7)**, so a socket listener records its file's
  device and inode as a `SocketClaim`: `shutdown` lets the drop run only
  while the claim `is_current`, and forgets the server otherwise; `release`
  (the quit path) unlinks only a current file and then forgets the whole
  listener — no unblock, no join — so a call in flight cannot hold a quit.
  The protocol revisions it negotiates are `mcp_versions.rs`'s, not its own.

  `LATEST_VERSION`) and `negotiate` (the requested one when supported, else
  the newest), moved out of `agent.rs` by road map 14's MC3 so ONE list
  serves two readers: `agent.rs`'s `initialize` and `mcp-proxy/`, which
  includes this file by `#[path]`. It therefore uses `std` alone and names
  nothing of this crate (no `use crate::…`).

  `ffi_agent.rs` has one slot, one listener per process: `SOCKET`
  (`rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`; MC4 deleted the TCP pair and its
  slot), whose `AgentConfig` is built by `host_config`, one catalog
  through one handler.
- `container.rs` · `container_header.rs` · `container_blocks.rs` ·

  is the first VP9 keyframe's header, each Opus packet's TOC and each Vorbis

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

1://! The op table — every op's ARGUMENTS, as data (spec §6).
2://!
3://! `edit.rs` owns what an op MEANS; this module owns what an op TAKES. One
4://! [`OpRow`] per op, in table order, and one [`Argument`] per argument: its
5://! name, its [`Kind`] and whether the decoder requires it. Nothing else is
6://! in a row — no prose, no semantics, and no default spelled a second time,
7://! because a default is what an absent argument MEANS and meaning is
8://! `edit.rs`'s doc table.
9://!
10://! It is a module of its own because the table is a published interface —
11://! the tool catalog will read it rather than restate it — while the [`Op`]
12://! enum and the sixty-four-way dispatch are the implementation of that
13://! interface. [`OP_NAMES`] is a projection of this table and is re-exported
14://! from `edit.rs` under its old name, so no caller anywhere moved.
15://!
16://! **Nothing here is the authority.** The `Op` enum's fields are, and
17://! `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves every row against them by asking the
18://! decoder: an argument the op does not have makes serde answer with the
19://! arguments it does have, an omitted required one makes it answer that the
20://! field is missing, and a value of the wrong kind makes it answer with the
21://! kind it wanted. A row that lies fails that test.
22://!
23://! ### The bound
24://!
25://! An argument may carry a [`Bound`], and the rule for one is narrow: **a
26://! bound the core REFUSES outside is published; a bound it CLAMPS to is
27://! not.** A published range is a promise a caller can build a call from,
28://! and a range that quietly corrects what it is handed would make that
29://! promise false in the one direction a caller could not see. So
30://! `set_canvas`'s two dimensions carry one — `edit_canvas.rs` refuses
31://! outside 16–16384 by name — and `set_speed`'s `rate`, which refuses a
32://! non-positive rate and then clamps to `SPEED_MIN`–`SPEED_MAX`, carries
33://! none: the clamp is the app's to say, in the tool prose that already says
34://! it.
35://!
36://! A bound is SOURCED from the constant that enforces it and never retyped
37://! here, which is what `core/tests/op_table.rs` checks by putting each end
38://! to the core and reading the refusal — including the numbers in it.
39://! A refused range that is not whole numbers (`set_track`'s `volume`
40://! 0–4 and `pan` −1–1) is stated in the tool's prose until [`Bound`]
41://! widens.
42://!
43://! ### The kinds
44://!
45://! The vocabulary is closed and spelled the way `edit.rs`'s argument column
46://! spelled it. **There is exactly one kind per answer the decoder can
47://! give**, which is the rule that says how many there are: two kinds serde
48://! refuses identically would be a distinction the table claims and no test
49://! could prove. So [`Kind::Ticks`], [`Kind::Number`], [`Kind::Boolean`],
50://! [`Kind::Text`], [`Kind::Texts`], [`Kind::Ids`] and [`Kind::Ranges`] are
51://! `Ticks`, `f64`, `bool`, `String`, `Vec<String>` (`set_action_end`'s
52://! `off` paths), `Vec<u32>` and the silence cut's `Vec<[Ticks; 2]>`, and
53://! the fifteen named types map like this:
54://!
55://! - [`Kind::Id`] — `u32`: an id naming a clip, track, action, marker or
56://!   media, and the canvas's two pixel dimensions, which are the same whole
57://!   non-negative number to a decoder and to a schema. [`Kind::Index`] is
58://!   `usize`, a place in the track stack, and is its own kind only because
59://!   serde names a different type in its refusal.
60://! - [`Kind::Color`] — `Color`, four numbers; [`Kind::FrameRate`] — `Fps`,

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);
a citation of the bare number names them together, and this index gets their rows in the same
change. Until #342 (2026-10-24) §4.3b was the Media, Document and Assistant tabs, now §4.3c; an older citation of §4.3b (in `archive/` or git history) means §4.3c.

The Lines column is `wc -l`; the `11-decisions/` cell is that folder's total, its README
included, and `make test` checks both (`tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`).

468:- **GR-9 — The branch wrote project format 1015 and refused 15–1014 by name; at the merge 1015
469-  became 15.** The branch's `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` was **1015** (main's 14 plus a thousand), in
470-  `core/src/format.rs` and the header, so every main build refused a branch-made project as "made
471-  by a newer Frame Job" instead of opening it and dropping its grades on the next save.
472-  Its base version was 14: the branch read 1 to 14 and 1015, and refused a file numbered 15 to
473-  1014 in its own sentence (naming the numbers it reads), because a later main file
474-  would otherwise open and lose its new keys on save (owner choice 9). Above 1015 the existing
475-  "newer" sentence answered. The branch had no migrate step: 1015 is 14 plus optional keys (and, since GR-6,
476-  the `adjustment` source kind, which an older build refuses by name). **At the merge** (GR7b,
477-  2026-10-10) 1015 became **15**, main's next version. A file numbered 1015 is read as 15 by one
478-  migration step (`migrate_1015_to_15` in `format.rs`, run before the "newer" gate, mapping to the
479-  literal 15 so a later bump still runs its own steps from 15; `GRADING_BRANCH_VERSION` names
480-  the number), so branch-made projects still open. The base-version constant and the gap refusal
481-  are gone, and 16 and above, 1014 included, are "newer". Risk accepted: a project the owner saved on
482-  the grading branch opened only there until the merge (he kept his trial projects as copies).
483-  **Amended by NM-5** (rename R0): the "newer" refusal's "update Reelcut to open it" is now "update
484-  Frame Job to open it", so "made by a newer Reelcut" is now "made by a newer Frame Job".

content.content:
**Stands, and nothing here re-litigates it:** R5-1 (closed vocabularies, never a runtime); G-1;
R5-5; §7.5's blending in encoded sRGB; MT-1..MT-9; PR-1..PR-5; "media by reference"; G-35.
**The Concat rule** (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, "Licensing") stands for every phase: tone's
formulas are textbook (the sRGB transfer functions of IEC 61966-2-1, Rec. 709 luma weights) and
Frame Job's own numbers, and nothing of Concat is opened, at design time or build time.

- **GR-1 — The grading experiment: tier 1 is IN, kept by the owner's verdict; tiers 2 and 3 are filed as issues.** Tier 1 is tone, adjustment clips, looks and `.cube` LUT import, with a way to see the
  grade: a before/after switch (View ▸ Show Ungraded, preview only) and one luma waveform. Flip and
  the shape mask leave the experiment (flip touches nothing about colour; a matte track over an
  adjustment clip does the mask's job). Wheels, curves, qualifiers, further scopes and the rest of
  tiers 2 and 3 are not OUT: they wait for the owner's verdict at GR7 (`archive/grading.md`, "Worth
  keeping"). **Amends spec §1**: its non-goal "color grading beyond per-clip controls" and the bar
  sentence's "scopes" no longer bind tier 1, and road map 2 §4's "LUTs (`.cube`)" exclusion
  (archived) is reversed by this entry. Risk accepted: the experiment costs the phases it takes,
  and a "no" leaves it unmerged. **Verdict (owner, 2026-10-10): kept**, merged into main; tiers 2
  and 3 are deferred as issues, not out. The owner: "I think we can merge this", and "T1 and T3
  look good to me. I'll get feedback later from others and we can adjust." T4 ran with test LUTs,
  not one of his own ("LUT worked"); T2, T5 and T6 were not run by him, and GRD-1…GRD-6 were not
  reported (they stay standing rows in `docs/manual-checks.md`, with GRD-7…GRD-10 added for T2,
  T5, T6 and other people's feedback).
- **GR-2 — Tone: nine keys under `video.color`, applied at step 4c behind a uniform flag;
  exposure and white balance in LOCAL linear light.**
  - The keys follow `hue` in this one order everywhere (the JSON, the uniforms, the inspector):
    `exposure` (−3…+3, in EV), `temperature`, `tint`, `highlights`, `shadows`, `whites`, `blacks`,
    `vibrance` (each −1…+1) and `fade` (0…1). Neutral is 0 for every one; a key is written only
    when not 0, so an untoned file's text is unchanged. Out of range is refused in the rule's own
    sentence (`video.color.exposure must be between -3 and 3, not 3.5`), never clamped by the
    patch; an action's end is clamped like the other colour keys. Set by `set_video {patch:
    {color: {…}}}` (no new op, no op-table row), animated by actions like every number (§5.4).
  - The strengths at ±1 are Frame Job's own (GR0's spike numbers, tunable at GR7): exposure ±1 is
    ×2 / ×½ on linear light; temperature ±1 is red ×2^±0.3 and blue ×2^∓0.3 on linear light; tint
    +1 is green ×2^−0.3 (towards magenta); highlights and shadows ±1 lift by ±0.25 weighted to the
    top and bottom halves of luma; whites and blacks ±1 stretch by ±15 % held at black and at
    white; vibrance ±1 scales saturation by 1 ± 1 on low-saturation colours and not at all at full
    saturation; fade 1 takes black to 10 % and white to 95 %.
  - **Step 4c** applies them once per pixel, after the obscure regions (4b) and before the point
    filters (5): obscured content is toned like the picture around it, and sepia and noir act on
    the toned colour. Exposure and the white-balance gains decode to linear light (IEC 61966-2-1),
    multiply, and re-encode INSIDE 4c; highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance and fade work
    on encoded values. This is a local colour transform like `hueRotate`: it does **not** amend
3:- **Status:** Built and closed 2026-10-10, kept by the owner's verdict and merged into main. Each phase was one litecode pipeline with its own review:

```sh
mkdir -p tools/proof/media && cd tools/proof/media
```

Phase 2 adds sound. The three movies above are silent, and a clip of a
silent movie has NO audio group (an `.m4a` clip has no video group), so the
solo proof needs two tones it can tell apart by ear and by byte, and the
paste-attributes proof needs one clip that has BOTH groups:

content.content:
- **AI-6 — W-9 governs automatic styling, not a person's request.** No PIPELINE picks words by
  meaning. The assistant writes a caption's text or style only because the person asked it to
  in the conversation, and each such edit is an ordinary undo step (§3g). Risk accepted: a
  person may ask for emphasis by meaning, which no pipeline may do.
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-5:** the same holds for cutting words. When the person asks,
  the assistant may choose words to cut by their meaning (a false start), reading them through
  `get_transcript`, a clip's words in timeline times that never makes a network call. It
  proposes, then makes ordinary undoable cuts; no pipeline picks words to cut by meaning.
- **AI-7 — What the assistant may not call, and what it must ask about first.** Withheld: the
  dev tools, always (V-1: they are not in Distribution, and the assistant sees one catalog in
  both builds); `record_screen`, always, because recording is a person at the Record button;
  and `transcribe` with the cloud engine, refused with R6-2's sentence and pointing at File ▸
  Generate Captions…. Ask first: `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project` and
  `consolidate_media`, because each writes files where the model chose (§3f, §6.3). Such a call
  is NOT run when the helper asks; the transcript shows a confirmation row naming the tool and
  where it writes, with Allow and Deny, and the helper's `tool_request` simply waits, so the
  helper is unchanged. Deny answers the call as an error, "The person declined: …". Stop,
  Clear, closing the window and a dead helper all answer a pending confirmation as declined.
  An MCP caller is never asked: the rule belongs to the assistant's lane, not to the tool. Both
  lists are one table in one file, with a "withheld" or "ask first" column and a reason on
  every row; the helper never sees a withheld tool, and the lane refuses one if it is called
  anyway. Risk accepted: recording and cloud transcription stay menu-only, and every file
  written costs a click.
  **Amended 2026-10-01, by #40**: `close_project` is withheld, always: closing a project
  closes the window the conversation lives in (AI-5).
  **Amended 2026-10-22, by TR-10**: `transcribe_for_fillers` is withheld, always, with R6-2's
  reason, pointing at Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…, which shows what is uploaded and what it costs.
- **AI-8 — The key is the person's own, and is R6-5 and R6-12's key in everything but the
  vendor.** It lives in `SecretStore` under `anthropic-key`; the one override is
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, read only as R6-5 amended says. It is never a tool argument, a launch
  argument or an answer, and is handed to the helper on stdin only (§1, §3i). R6-9's
  `-RCSecretFolder` keeps proofs away from the person's file. R6-5's "integrated AI offering"
  is THIS, and it does not unblock C2 (#125), which still needs the caller's identity. Risk
  accepted: a `0600` file rather than the Keychain, for R6-5's measured reason.

content.content:
# Manual checks

The standing list of checks only a person at the machine can do: things
that need eyes, ears, a real mouse and keyboard, a second display, a real
network, a real API key or macOS permissions. Everything a script can
measure is already in `tools/proof/` and is not repeated here.

**When to run it.** Run every section before a release. Between releases,
run the sections whose area changed. Unless a check says otherwise, run it
in both appearances (System Settings ▸ Appearance, Light then Dark).

## Setup, once per run

1. Build: `make app`.
2. Open the Release app from the Finder, or with
   `open "build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app"`. **Not from a terminal**:
   a terminal-launched app's permissions (Screen Recording, Microphone)
   belong to the terminal, not to Frame Job. Only REC-3, REC-7, REC-8's
   step 6 and HS-2 launch from a terminal on purpose.
3. Have to hand:
   - **Real footage**: a 1080p movie with sound, a long recording (twenty
     minutes or more), an AAC file and a WAV file.
   - **Synthetic test media**, where a check names it: make it once with the
     `ffmpeg` lines under "Make the test media once" in
     `tools/proof/README.md` (into `tools/proof/media/`).
   - **Graphics projects** (GR): `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphics_playback_samples.py`
     builds `Playback-1080p`, `Playback-4K`, `Error-card` and
     `Playback-4K-animated` into `tools/proof/work/playback-check/`. Rebuild them on a fresh checkout.
   - **Keys**: your own AssemblyAI key for Cloud captions (Frame Job ▸
     Settings… ▸ Transcription) and your own Anthropic API key for the
     Assistant (Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant). No script ever uses a real
     key.
4. **The compositor's timing log** (PB-2, PB-3):
   `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob FrameJobCompositorTiming -bool YES`,
   relaunch, and read it in Console.app filtered on `[framejob] compositor`
   (average and worst milliseconds per 120 frames). Turn it off afterwards
   with `defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob FrameJobCompositorTiming`.

## Reporting a failure
